articles.title: Discovering new antibiotics with ChatGPT
articles.summary: The de la Fuente Lab is using ChatGPT and Codex in the search for new molecules that could help fight antibiotic-resistant bacteria.
body: Modern medicine relies on effective antibiotics, which help us recover from routine illnesses, surgeries, childbirth, and more. However, antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a growing problem. Approximately 5 million people die every year from bacterial AMR, and that number is expected to double by 2050. Dr. César de la Fuente and his team use ChatGPT and Codex to explore the genetic code of living and extinct organisms like woolly mammoths, snake venom, and more to identify promising antibiotic molecules. Work that traditionally takes five or six years can now be done in a matter of hours.
points: The de la Fuente Lab is using ChatGPT and Codex in the search for new molecules that could help fight antibiotic-resistant bacteria.

articles.summary: ChatGPT Work is now powered by GPT-6 Astra—our best model for professional work.
body: Bring it your next big project. With Astra, ChatGPT Work better understands what you’re trying to do and pulls together the information you need from your connected apps and computer. It helps you create polished reports, presentations, and analyses faster—with more natural writing, a closer fit to your templates and style, and less cleanup.

Then hand over the busywork. With your permission, ChatGPT Work can use your desktop apps and browser much like you do—clicking, typing, and moving between screens to fill out forms, update records and trackers, and schedule meetings. Astra makes it better and faster at these tasks, even in apps that don’t have a ChatGPT integration.
